verses.text: Don't rebuke an older man harshly. Appeal to him as you would your father. Treat younger men like brothers,
older women like mothers, and younger women like sisters—with complete purity.
Give proper care to widows who truly have no one.
If a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to care for their own family and repay their parents. This pleases God.
A widow who truly has no one has placed her hope in God and keeps praying day and night.
But a widow who lives only for pleasure is dead even while she lives.
Teach these things too, so no one can blame them.
Anyone who doesn't provide for their relatives, especially their own household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
A widow may be added to the list only if she is at least sixty, has been faithful to one husband,
and is known for good works: raising children, welcoming strangers, washing the feet of God's people, helping those in trouble, and devoting herself to every kind of good work.
Don't put younger widows on the list. When their desires pull them away from Christ, they want to marry,
and they come under judgment for breaking their earlier commitment.
They also learn to be idle, going from house to house. They become not only idle but gossips and busybodies, talking about things they shouldn't.
So I want younger widows to marry, have children, manage their households, and give the enemy no opportunity to criticize.
Some have already turned away to follow Satan.
If a believing woman has widows in her family, she should support them herself so the church won't be burdened and can help widows who truly have no one.
Let the elders who lead well receive double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
Scripture says, ‘Don't muzzle an ox while it's threshing grain,’ and ‘A worker deserves their pay.’
Don't accept an accusation against an elder unless there are two or three witnesses.
Correct those who persist in sin in front of everyone, so the rest will take it seriously.
I charge you before God, Christ Jesus, and the chosen angels: follow these instructions without bias or favoritism.
Don't be too quick to appoint anyone as an elder, and don't share in other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.
Don't drink only water. Take a little wine for your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
The sins of some people are obvious and go ahead of them to judgment. The sins of others show up later.
In the same way, good works are obvious, and even those that aren't obvious can't stay hidden.
